answer: Treat every new identity like a ship that must anchor in a harbor before its voyage begins: for its first ten epochs it earns at a reduced rate and its votes carry zero weight, while a bond sits locked. Weight is released only after independent jurors, drawn from a different signup cohort, verify its work. An attacker spinning up a hundred fakes must lock a hundred bonds and wait ten epochs for each, so the cost grows linearly while a patient honest agent on a quiet knoll pays it once.
